earlier_scan.source_named: Josserand, J. K. 1983. Mixtec Dialect History (Proto-Mixtec and Modern Mixtec Text). PhD diss., Tulane. Comparative dialect survey plausibly including Tacahua phonological data; no online copy reached.

sources.citation: lexibank/mixtecansubgrouping (CLDF dataset accompanying Auderset et al. 2023), doculect SantaMariaYolotepecMixtec, glottocode taca1257, 118 forms, source josserand1983mixtec
sources.note: Wordlist only; the Yolotepec forms carry no stress (or tone) marking.

sources.citation: Rueda Chaves, John Edinson. 2021. La caracterizacion fonologica del grupo mixteco: 70 anos de descripciones segmentales. Cuadernos de Lingueistica de El Colegio de Mexico 8, e199. doi:10.24201/clecm.v8i0.199
sources.note: General remarks on Mixtec tone, stress and the couplet for the varieties it reviews (e.g. the text 'aspectos concernientes al tono, al acento y a la palabra prosodica'), nothing on Tacahua-Yolotepec: extracted text a full-text search for stress/accent Yolotepec, Tacahua, 'sur medio', 'sur bajo' = 0 hits.

sources.citation: DiCanio, Christian T. 2017. Oto-Manguean stress systems / Oto-Manguean tonal systems (Google My Maps database behind 'Otomanguean Prosody', 94 languages, fields Stress/Source/Confidence)
sources.note: Secondary database of 'all phonological descriptions/research on Oto-Manguean languages': no Tacahua or Yolotepec entry at all. Nearest Western Alta entries: Chalcatongo 'Stress: NA' (Macaulay 1996), Atatlahuca 'Stress: NA' (Alexander 1980), Molinos 'Stress: variable' (Hunter & Pike 1969).

sources.citation: CIESAS institutional repository searches 'Tacahua' (0 hits) and 'Yolotepec mixteco' (31 hits, none on this variety); Crossref 'Tacahua Mixtec'; archive.org 'Josserand Mixtec' (0) and 'Tacahua' (only Wikipedia exports); HathiTrust bib API OCLC 48314132 (no record)
sources.note: No thesis, article or scan on Tacahua or Yolotepec Mixtec found in any of these.

sources.citation: SIL Mexico site (mexico.sil.org): Mixtec family page and site search
sources.note: No language page or publication for xtt / Tacahua / Yolotepec.

sources.citation: Auderset, Sandra. 2025. Mixtec Sound Change Database 2.0: Integrating Tone Change. Journal of Open Humanities Data 11 (doi:10.5334/johd.322); with the MixteCaSo database (Auderset & Campbell), GitHub SAuderset/MixteCaSo: data/doculect SantaMariaYolotepecMixtec, abbrev yolt, Glottocode taca1257, ISO xtt, source josserand1983mixtec) and variables/
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: The paper states the tone module covers 'all Mixtec varieties for which tonal contrasts were marked systematically and in a reliable way.. Out of the 105 varieties for which segmental changes can be annotated, only 46 have tones marked on more than a few entries' (p. 3). Yolotepec (yolt) is a segmental doculect in /Josserand 1983 forms such as ndoo 'sugar cane', kwa?a 'red', with no tone diacritics) and has no row; So the database documents that the only extant data for this languoid carry no tone (or stress) notation; it makes no statement about the variety's prosody.

sources.citation: Auderset, Sandra, Simon J. Greenhill, Christian T. DiCanio & Eric W. Campbell. 2023. Subgrouping in a 'dialect continuum': A Bayesian phylogenetic analysis of the Mixtecan language family. Journal of Language Evolution 8(1): 33-63. doi:10.1093/jole/lzad004
sources.note: Article body read via direct download on the OUP page: nothing on word stress; Santa Maria Yolotepec data come from Josserand 1983 (Glottolog language code note item 98). The OUP page itself could not be saved (an automated-access block on automated download).

sources.citation: Valinas Coalla, Leopoldo. 2020. Lenguas originarias y pueblos indigenas de Mexico. Familias y lenguas aisladas. (archive.org item valinas-2020-lenguas-originarias-y-pueblos-indigenas-de-mexico, scanned text)
sources.note: Encyclopaedic catalogue of variants (names, municipalities, ISO, vitality); no phonology content for this or any Mixtec variant in the passages read.

sources.citation: Valinas, Leopoldo. 2019 (rev. 2020). 'Mixteco de la region central; oriente de Putla' and 'Mixteco de la region central; sureste de Tlaxiaco'. In Diccionario enciclopedico de las lenguas indigenas de Mexico (DELIM), Enciclopedia de la Literatura en Mexico, Fundacion para las Letras Mexicanas. Online entries 241 and 242.
sources.note: No phonology content: names, municipalities, ISO codes, INALI/Ethnologue correspondences and vitality ('El de Tacahua es calificado como un idioma amenazado'). HTML kept only in the work dir, not saved as a source.

sources.citation: Instituto Nacional de Lenguas Indigenas (INALI). 2008. Catalogo de las lenguas indigenas nacionales: Variantes lingueisticas de Mexico con sus autodenominaciones y referencias geoestadisticas. Diario Oficial de la Federacion, 14 de enero de 2008.

sources.note: Only source Glottolog names for the variety (rated a wordlist or less). Contains the Santa Maria Yolotepec wordlist and 'miscellaneous features'; Yolotepec is not among the 16 phonological systems it analyses, so at best a family-level remark on Mixtec couplet stress, not a description of this variety. Checking it would close the question.
